moments.title: Naomi Osaka withdraws from French Open
moments.body: On 31 May 2021, Naomi Osaka withdraws from the French Open after being fined for skipping press conferences citing mental health. She discloses long-running depression and social anxiety. The Grand Slam tournaments respond with restructured media obligations.
moments.takeaway: A reigning Grand Slam champion declining mandatory press obligations forced sport governance to take mental health seriously.

moments.title: Simone Biles withdraws from Tokyo
moments.body: On 27 July 2021, Simone Biles withdraws from the Olympic team final after experiencing 'twisties' — disorientation in mid-air, potentially career-ending for a gymnast. She wins bronze on beam later in the Games. She returns to competition in 2023 and wins three more Olympic golds at Paris 2024.
moments.takeaway: The most decorated gymnast in history publicly declined a competition for mental health and physical safety — and was largely supported.

now.title: Athlete welfare today
now.body: Mental health support staff are now standard at major sporting events. Major leagues (NBA, NHL, NFL) have dedicated programmes. The IOC introduced a Mental Health Action Plan (2021). Survivor advocacy (Larry Nassar case in US gymnastics) and FA's 2022 inquiry into historical child abuse have changed safeguarding standards.
now.open_questions: How do training cultures change to support, not just permit, vulnerability disclosure?

reflection: A generation of professional athletes was conditioned to play through pain. The current shift — that athlete welfare can outrank competition — represents a substantive change in sport culture. Whether it's permanent is unclear.
